# Babble Engine

> Babble Engine turns a line of text into gibberish speech for game characters: made-up language, critter chatter, robot beeps and soft tones. It runs in the browser, is free, and is made by Wrong Floor.

Babble Engine is for game developers who want characters to "talk" without voice acting. You type a line, pick a style and a voice, listen, and export a WAV file. You can also record your own voice in the studio and use it as the source for the babble. The Script tab keeps a game's dialogue (scenes, characters, recorded and babble lines) and exports a zip with a WAV per line plus script.json. Recordings stay in the browser (IndexedDB); nothing is uploaded and there are no accounts.

## Use it

- [Babble Engine](https://babble.wrongfloor.studio/): the tool, in English and Dutch
- [Use it in your game](https://babble.wrongfloor.studio/game): the same engine as one JavaScript file, with examples
- [Source code on GitHub](https://github.com/wrongfloor-dev/babble-engine): plain HTML and JavaScript, no dependencies

## Styles

16 styles. Voice styles (work with your own recorded voice): Critter Chatter, Babblish, Bloopa Doopa, Name Talk, Grunts & Barks, Grumble, Gizmo, Sprite, Spooky Whisper, Echo Folk, Mumble Radio, Babytalk. Sound styles (no voice): Text Blips, Droid Chirps, Soft Tones, Talking Instruments (with a kazoo).

## Web module (for game code)

One ES module, no build step, no dependencies, no server. Works in the browser; `render` and `toWav` also run in Node (`require('./site/src/engine.js')`).

```js
import { render, play, toWav, styles, loadVoice } from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/wrongfloor-dev/babble-engine@1/site/src/babble.mjs';

const line = render('Hi! Do you want an apple?', { style: 'animal', voice: 'fern', mood: 'happy' });
const p = play(line);   // browser only, with the style's room; returns { stop(), ended, context }
p.stop();               // stop it, e.g. when the next dialogue line starts
line.syllables;         // [{ time, text }]: syllable start times in seconds, for mouth flaps or subtitles
toWav(line);            // ArrayBuffer, 16-bit mono WAV, dry
```

render(text, options) returns { pcm (Float32Array, mono, dry), sampleRate, duration, syllables, style, voice }. Options:

- style: default 'animal'. voice: default the style's first voice
- mood: neutral, happy, angry, sad, flirty, surprised (default neutral)
- seed: default 1. Same text, options and seed give the same sound
- sampleRate: default 48000
- pitch, speed, expression, throat, breath, brightness: override the voice
- hiss: 0 to 1, consonant noise
- name: Name Talk only, the name the creature keeps saying (like 'Pikachu')
- intent, length: Bloopa Doopa only (style 'vemmo'). It ignores the text and speaks by intent: greet, bye, tell, explain, ask, curious, joy, cheer, think, letdown, agree, warn. length 'short' or 'medium'
- ownVoice, steady: a voice from loadVoice(), exported in the tool under Voices & characters as a .babble-voice.json file. Voice styles only

Unknown styles, voices, moods or intents throw an Error whose message starts with 'Babble: ' and lists the valid values.

## Godot 4 addon

Download https://github.com/wrongfloor-dev/babble-engine/releases/latest/download/babble-engine-godot.zip and unzip it in the project folder, or install it from the Godot Asset Library (https://godotengine.org/asset-library/asset/5567, AssetLib tab: search "Babble Engine"), or copy addons/babble_engine from the GitHub repo; no plugin to enable. A BabbleSpeaker node (an AudioStreamPlayer with style, voice, mood, babble_seed, options and own_voice_file) renders on a background thread and plays the line: speak(text), stop_line(), signals line_started(text), syllable(index, text) and line_finished. BabbleEngine.render(text, options) takes the same options in snake_case (sample_rate, own_voice) and gives the same samples as the web module; a bad option prints an error and returns {}. BabbleEngine.load_voice(text) reads a .babble-voice.json.

## Style and voice ids

- `animal` Critter Chatter: `fern`, `burt`, `pip`, `lowell`, `bleep`
- `sim` Babblish: `lottie`, `ben`, `kiki`, `hank`, `whisper`, `bubs`
- `vemmo` Bloopa Doopa: `jesse`, `bram`, `mila`
- `name` Name Talk: `moki`, `grumbo`, `zee`, `lulu`, `bonk`
- `bark` Grunts & Barks: `hero`, `heroine`, `elder`, `kid`, `brute`
- `grumble` Grumble: `grok`, `moss`, `burly`
- `gizmo` Gizmo: `bolt`, `cog`, `unit9`
- `sprite` Sprite: `fae`, `wisp`, `glimmer`
- `ghost` Spooky Whisper: `whisper`, `wail`, `hollow`
- `echo` Echo Folk: `village`, `crowd`, `kids`
- `radio` Mumble Radio: `dispatch`, `pilot`, `scout`
- `baby` Babytalk: `tot`, `bubba`, `mini`
- `blip` Text Blips (no own voice): `pixel`, `tiny`, `boss`, `soft`, `typewriter`
- `droid` Droid Chirps (no own voice): `beebo`, `rollo`, `zapp`, `mini`
- `tone` Soft Tones (no own voice): `clouds`, `softbubble`, `rain`, `breeze`, `hum`, `purr`, `wood`, `droplet`, `kalimba`, `felt`, `bubble`, `glass`
- `instr` Talking Instruments (no own voice): `horn`, `trombone`, `choir`, `kazoo`

## Script files (the Script tab of the tool)

The Script tab keeps a game's dialogue: scenes, characters, lines, recorded takes and babble lines. Import a script file there (⋯ › Import), or paste plain text: `# Scene` starts a scene, `Name: text` is a line, `Name (direction): text` adds a direction.

A script file `<title>.babble-script.json`:

```json
{ "format": "babble-script", "version": 1, "title": "Tutorial", "lang": "en",
  "scenes": ["Arrival"],
  "characters": [
    { "id": "guide", "name": "Guide", "kind": "record" },
    { "id": "shop", "name": "Shopkeeper", "kind": "babble", "style": "animal", "voice": "burt", "mood": "happy",
      "fx": { "pitch": 0, "effect": "", "room": "none" } }
  ],
  "lines": [
    { "id": "l1", "scene": "Arrival", "character": "guide", "dir": "cheerful", "text": "Hello there!" },
    { "id": "l2", "scene": "Arrival", "character": "shop", "text": "[Welcome!] What can I get you?" }
  ] }
```

- `kind`: `record` (you speak the lines) or `babble` (`style`, `voice`, `mood`, or `intent` for `vemmo`, as in the web module)
- `character` in a line: a character id or name. Keep line ids when you change a file: importing syncs on `id`, a changed text puts the line on "redo" and keeps its takes; lines without an id are matched on character and text
- A babble line can have one part in [square brackets] that is spoken or recorded; the rest babbles
- `fx` (optional, sound of the takes): `pitch` -12 to 12 semitones (higher also plays faster), `effect` `""`, `radio`, `gizmo` (robot), `sprite` (fairy) or `grumble` (troll), `room` `none`, `small` or `big`

Export › For your game gives a zip: one `<line id>.wav` per line (sound and room included) and `script.json`:
`{ format: "babble-script-export", version: 1, title, lang, sampleRate, lines: [{ id, scene, character, characterId, text, dir?, file, duration, babble?, mixed?, spoken?, syllables? }] }`.
`file` is null for a line without a take. `babble` holds the web module options (with `seed`), so a game can also render that line live; `syllables` is `[{ time, text }]` for a babble line.
